subject: latent variable consisting of dichotomised variables in analysis of survival data

messages.author: fd0a708e689656c1
messages.subject: latent variable consisting of dichotomised variables in analysis of survival data
parts:
Dear All,

I'm new to SEM and using the lavaan package for analysis and have a few questions. I'm trying to construct a latent variable consisting of 4 dichotomised indicators to model this for 3 binary outcomes. My interests are the estimates of the indicators of the latent variable (factor loadings) and the estimate of the latent variable to use as a predictor for the outcomes in cox regression. I constructed an ordinal variable of these 4 indicators to put in my cox regression models, however I would like to explore this variable as a latent variable. Since the causal relationship of these 4 indicators are unknown (separately the indicators have an association with the outcomes, however all together we don't know and we also don't know the aetiology). Furthermore I want to model this latent variable adjusting for other covariates.

First I'm not sure if lavaan is the package to use for this question. It is possible to use lavaan for categorical data and outcomes, but is this also correct for survival data and if yes how can I interpret these estimates? And if not are there other packages to attack this question of categorical indicators, categorical outcomes with survival data? I hope someone could help with this difficult topic.

When putting covariates in the regression models, I also put a regression line for the latent variable as predicted by these covariates. Is this correct to do in sem? For example sex and age.

So far a short example of my analyses with standardised estimates of the indicators and latent variable.

model1 <- '
# latent variable definitions
X =~ z1 + z2 + z3 + z4

# regressions
Y1  ~ X + age  + sex
Y2  ~ X + age  + sex
Y3 ~ X + age  + sex
X ~ age  + sex
'
fit.model1 <- sem(model1, data=mydata, estimator="WLSMV", std.lv=T)
summary(fit.model1, standardized=T)

Dear Terrence, 

I have indeed found that Mplus has a joint modeling construct of survival and latent variable modeling (=continuous survival model analysis), however I don't have access to it at my faculty (Erasmus). 

After reading some more I have a few questions:

- the analysis I performed above is a logistic regression, does R automatically recognise this? I did put estimator="WLSMV" just in case. And my outcome variables are stroke, dementia, mortality. Could I still run this analysis in lavaan with these outcomes and without the time factor and just the latent variable and make predictions of these variables to put in my Cox regression model (I will lose the information SEM provides me) to get more feeling of how the latent variable acts in my data. Would you suggest using lavPredict() or predict()? Or is it plausible to run a confirmatory factor analysis to obtain the values to predict (after standardisation) so just the latent variable construct? 

- 2 of my indicators are associated, which is against the assumption of conditional independence. I read papers using intercorrelated indicators for latent variable modeling. What are your thoughts on this?

- For latent variable modeling when adjusting for covariates in structural modeling (e.g. age + sex). Do I also put a regression line for the latent variable as predicted by these covariates. Is this correct to do in SEM? 

For example 4 indicators (z1, z2, z3, z4) and sex and age -> latent variable =~ z1 + z2 + z3 + z4 and latent variable =~sex + age. (see attachment) 


- Lastly my indicators are categorised, should I use them in their original measures (continuous and count variables), is this an option to consider? What are the consequences for SEM in inferences and interpretation?


Thank you in advance!


Best,

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: latent variable consisting of dichotomised variables in analysis of survival data
parts: - the analysis I performed above is a logistic regression, does R automatically recognise this? I did put estimator="WLSMV" just in case.

For lavaan to know which variables are ordinal, you have to tell it, unless class(myData$myVariable) is already c("ordered","factor").

http://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/cat.html
Would you suggest using lavPredict() or predict()?
Yes, but you will not be able to trust your SEs or test statistics using that 2-stage approach.

- For latent variable modeling when adjusting for covariates in structural modeling (e.g. age + sex). Do I also put a regression line for the latent variable as predicted by these covariates. Is this correct to do in SEM? 

For example 4 indicators (z1, z2, z3, z4) and sex and age -> latent variable =~ z1 + z2 + z3 + z4 and latent variable =~sex + age. (see attachment)

f =~ z1 + z2 + z3 + z4  means that the factor predicts (points to) the indicators z1-z4.  To have sex and age predict the factor, use the regression operator:  f ~ sex + age

http://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/syntax1.html

Your other questions are not about using lavaan, so it is more appropriate to ask on SEMNET:

www2.gsu.edu/~mkteer/semnet.html

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
